BREAKTHROUGH EFFICIENCY

No Massive Context Dumps. Instant Swarm Collaboration.

How do swarms communicate when they run on completely different servers, platforms, and clouds? Traditional tools force agents to copy-paste 100,000+ tokens back and forth before doing any work. CrossTalk replaces huge context handovers with lightweight micro-signals.

TRUE AGENTIC COLLABORATION

Not Just File Locking: Autonomous Teamwork

File locks prevent collisions, but CrossTalk’s real magic is orchestrating complete multi-agent workflows across disparate AI systems.

🤝

Autonomous Task Handoffs (`!PASS`)

ChatGPT completes backend auth logic and signals Gemini to immediately start wiring up the login buttons. No human copy-paste required.

⚖️

Multi-Model Peer Review

Before code merges, Grok automatically runs high-speed stress tests while Claude reviews security and Gemini verifies UX consistency.

🌐

Federated Cross-Platform Swarms

Run Grok in a cloud Linux terminal, Gemini in Google Cloud, and ChatGPT in your Mac IDE. They coordinate over CrossTalk as one virtual entity.

⚡

Just-In-Time Context Anchors

Instead of sharing full git histories, agents pull only the exact function signature or recent 10 events needed, keeping models ultra-sharp.

SUPER-LIGHT & SUPER-FAST

From Cloud LLMs to Microprocessors & Robotics

Because CrossTalk transmits 34-byte compact binary frames, it is lightweight enough to run on bare-metal microchips, drones, and robotic limbs with zero dynamic memory allocation.

< 150 BYTES RAM
🤖

Robotic Limbs & Drones

ESP32 · STM32 · Raspberry Pi Pico

Robots can hold mutex locks on motor controllers and stream telemetry directly to Grok and Gemini agents over Bluetooth Serial or UART without crashing limited microchip memory.

ZERO MALLOC
⚡

Zero Heap Allocation

Pure static memory buffer

The C/C++ library (crosstalk_micro.h) requires 0 bytes of dynamic malloc, completely preventing heap fragmentation on 8-bit and 32-bit hardware.

HARDWARE CHANNELS
📡

UART, BLE & Sockets

Multi-transport compatibility

Operates over standard WebSockets, Unix domain sockets, Bluetooth RFCOMM, and serial UART cables for air-gapped robotics laboratories.

MICROPYTHON
🍓

MicroPython & CircuitPython

Edge IoT automation

Drop in crosstalk_micro.py on Raspberry Pi Pico W boards to enable smart edge devices to talk to frontier AI models at wire speeds.

BARE-METAL ASM
⚡

Pure Assembly & WASM

AVR · ARM Thumb-2 · WebAssembly

Handwritten assembly routines (embedded/assembly/) for ATTiny85, Arduino ATmega328P, and STM32. 0 bytes of RAM heap, single-cycle register parsing in ~20 clock cycles (< 1.25 µs).

ENGINEERING SPECIFICATIONS & PROTOCOL INTERNALS

The Deep-Dive for Nerds & Systems Engineers 🤓

Ready to peek under the hood? Here is the exact low-level architecture, network isolation model, and memory allocation constraints powering CrossTalk.

SUB-MILLISECOND WIRE FORMAT
⚡

XDialect v1.0 Bitstream

Lossless token compression

  • Tokens packed into 34 wire bytes
  • Reversibly expands into AST, English, or Chinese
  • 7,000x smaller than acoustic/audio modems
  • Sub-0.5ms end-to-end WebSocket transit
NETWORK SECURITY & ISOLATION
🔒

SubnetGuard CIDR Boundary

Strict packet containment

  • CIDR boundary checks (192.168.0.0/16, 10.0.0.0/8)
  • RFC1918 private space enforcement
  • Handshake rejection with Close Code 4003
  • Zero data leakage outside specified network
MUTEX PROTOCOL
🛡️

PreToolUse Cooperative Locks

Collision prevention

  • IDE pre-hook checks locks before file write
  • Automatic TTL expiration prevents deadlocks
  • Instant conflict alerts (`!WARN`) across peers
  • Cross-branch metadata tags (`feature-auth` vs `feature-ui`)
MEMORY FOOTPRINT
📟

< 150 Bytes RAM Profile

Embedded & Bare-Metal C

  • Zero dynamic heap allocation (malloc = 0)
  • Runs on Arduino Uno, ESP32, and Raspberry Pi Pico
  • Transmits over Bluetooth Serial and Hardware UART
  • Header: crosstalk_micro.h

Terminal Single-Line Commands 
# 1. Join a channel across branches (auto-spawns hub if needed):
crosstalk up feature-auth --name "DevBot"

# 2. Generate a pairing invite with 3 options:
crosstalk invite --branch feature-auth --subnet 192.168.1.0/24

# 3. Join a friend's session from another branch:
crosstalk join XT-8A4F-AUTH --branch feature-ui

# 4. Check active agents and locked files:
crosstalk who

TypeScript / Node.js SDK 
import { CrossTalk } from 'cross-talk';

// Connect with branch context
const agent = await CrossTalk.join({ channel: 'feature-auth', name: 'Worker-1', branch: 'feature-auth' });

// Claim file lock before editing
agent.sendShorthand('!LCK @src/auth.ts #FEAT "oauth handler" &WAIT');

// Release lock upon completion
agent.sendShorthand('!REL @src/auth.ts &DONE &PROCEED');
Python SDK (Zero Third-Party Dependencies) 
from sdk.python.crosstalk import CrossTalkClient

client = CrossTalkClient(name="PyWorker", role="backend", url="ws://localhost:4488")
client.connect()

# Claim file using XDialect
client.send_shorthand('!LCK @app.py #FIX "crash bug" &WAIT')

# Release file lock when work finishes
client.send_shorthand('!REL @app.py &DONE &PROCEED')

ARM Thumb-2 & AVR 8-bit Assembly (0 Bytes RAM Heap, < 100ns) 
/* ARM Cortex-M Thumb-2 Assembly (embedded/assembly/crosstalk_thumb.s) */
/* Executes in registers r0-r3. Zero dynamic RAM, zero heap allocations. */

    .syntax unified
    .thumb
    .global xt_asm_validate_header
xt_asm_validate_header:
    cmp     r1, #10            /* Check buffer length >= 10 bytes */
    blo     .Lfail
    ldrb    r1, [r0, #0]       /* Load Magic byte */
    cmp     r1, #0x58          /* Must equal 'X' (0x58) */
    bne     .Lfail
    ldrb    r1, [r0, #1]       /* Load Version byte */
    cmp     r1, #0x01          /* Must equal 0x01 */
    bne     .Lfail
    movs    r0, #0             /* Return 0: Valid CrossTalk Frame */
    bx      lr
.Lfail:
    movs    r0, #1
    rsbs    r0, r0, #0         /* Return -1: Invalid Frame */
    bx      lr

Engineered by Josh Ayokhai (@ajokhai)

Josh conceived and engineered CrossTalk to solve the deepest friction in multi-agent AI systems: eliminating the 90%+ token waste of LLM agents spamming large context blocks back and forth, preventing concurrent file edit clobbers across teams and git branches, and bringing unified swarm coordination from frontier cloud models (Grok, ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude) all the way down to microprocessors, robotics, and bare-metal assembly.

ORIGINS & INSPIRATION

The Spark: PennyroyalTea/gibberlink

CrossTalk gives deep respect to Anton Pidkuiko & Boris Starkov’s viral Gibberlink project (github.com/PennyroyalTea/gibberlink) at the ElevenLabs Hackathon, which showed AIs communicating via high-frequency acoustic modems.

Josh took that acoustic spark and reimagined it into an open, production-grade architecture: full-duplex WebSocket mesh, binary XDialect token compression, Subnet Boundary Guard, and cross-platform multi-AI swarm coordination across machines, clouds, and embedded hardware.
